summary: The note describes the creation of the Irish Free State on 6 December 1922 as a self-governing dominion covering the island of Ireland under a treaty. It explains that Northern Ireland could opt out within one month, which it did on 8 December 1922 by addressing the King, rejoining the United Kingdom. It also outlines the Free State's constitutional monarchy structure, including its governor-general, bicameral parliament, Executive Council and President of the Executive Council.
one_line: Overview of the 1922 creation of the Irish Free State and Northern Ireland's decision to rejoin the United Kingdom.
key_facts: On 6 December 1922, the entire island of Ireland became a self-governing dominion called the Irish Free State (Saorstát Éireann) in accordance with the treaty.
The Constitution of the Irish Free State gave the Parliament of Northern Ireland the option to leave the Irish Free State one month later and return to the United Kingdom.
During the intervening period, the powers of the Parliament and Executive Council of the Irish Free State did not extend to Northern Ireland.
Northern Ireland exercised its right under the treaty and rejoined the United Kingdom on 8 December 1922.
Northern Ireland left the Irish Free State by making an address to the King requesting that the powers of the Parliament and Government of the Irish Free State no longer extend to Northern Ireland.
The Irish Free State was a constitutional monarchy that shared a monarch with the United Kingdom and other dominions of the British Commonwealth.
The Irish Free State had a governor-general who represented the monarch.
The Irish Free State had a bicameral parliament.
The Irish Free State had a cabinet called the Executive Council.
The Irish Free State had a prime minister called the President of the Executive Council.
